fields.name: Relay
fields.summary: AI workflow automation tool built as a Zapier alternative.
fields.narrative: Relay let users automate email and task workflows with AI agents, but as OpenAI, Google, and other larger platforms built similar automation directly into their own tools, the five-year-old startup struggled to hold on to a reason to exist as a stand-alone product. Lesson: agent features are being absorbed by the platforms they run on.

fields.name: Character.ai
fields.summary: Custom AI character chat app; raised $150M at a $1B valuation.
fields.narrative: Founded by ex-Google researchers, buzzed-about, then hollowed out: Google paid a reported $2.7B to license the tech and rehire the founders, lawsuits alleged chatbots contributed to teen harm, Disney sent a cease-and-desist. Filed for bankruptcy in October 2026 citing legal, regulatory, and operational headwinds. In an ironic twist, Disney is the opening bidder ($20M IP license).

fields.name: Sora
fields.summary: OpenAI's video-sharing platform; killed by costs and retention.
fields.narrative: Sora struggled with high operating costs and user-retention challenges and shut down in March 2026. Lesson: video generation infrastructure is brutally expensive to run as a consumer destination.

fields.name: ChatGPT Atlas
fields.summary: Standalone AI browser by OpenAI; lasted less than a year.
fields.narrative: Discontinued August 9 with its most useful features folded into ChatGPT. OpenAI has folded Operator in the same way and is shrinking DALL-E's standalone role.

fields.name: OpenAI Super App Redesign
fields.summary: Attempt to turn ChatGPT into a 'super app'; rolled back after backlash.
fields.narrative: The July 9 update combined Chat, Codex, and Work modes and renamed the classic UI 'ChatGPT Classic'. Users found it confusing and cluttered; OpenAI rolled it back. Lesson: familiarity is a feature.

fields.name: Apple Siri AI
fields.summary: Promised with Apple Intelligence in 2024; shipped ~2 years late.
fields.narrative: Repeated pushbacks citing engineering issues and bugs contributed to a $250M settlement over iPhone 16 AI marketing claims. The new Siri reached the iOS 27 beta in July 2026 and English users in October 2026.

fields.name: Microsoft Recall
fields.summary: AI 'photographic memory' for Windows; delayed ~1 year over privacy backlash.
fields.narrative: Periodic screenshots of everything users do triggered an immediate privacy and security backlash. Even after a redesign, a researcher built a tool extracting Recall's captured data, reviving questions about whether the underlying problem is fixed.

fields.name: Notion Mail
fields.summary: AI-focused email product; users chose other AI agents instead.
fields.narrative: Launched April 2025 to organize and automate inboxes; Notion noticed users handling email with separate AI agents instead. Scheduled to shut down September 22. Lesson: watch what users do, not what they ask for.

fields.name: Humane AI Pin
fields.summary: AI wearable; $230M raised, assets sold to HP for $116M.
fields.narrative: Probably the most famous AI hardware failure. Struggled with performance, then warned customers to stop using its charging case over battery-fire risk. HP acquired the assets for $116M — a partial Lifeboat rescue.

fields.name: Rabbit R1
fields.summary: Hyped AI companion device; sold 100K units, reviewed as unfinished.
fields.narrative: Strong initial sales didn't mean a strong product. Rabbit kept updating the R1, repositioned it as a computer controller for agentic tasks, and announced 'Project Cyberdeck' — a portable vibe-coding device. A pivot, not a death (yet).

fields.name: Huxe
fields.summary: AI audio app by ex-NotebookLM devs; outcompeted by Spotify et al.
fields.narrative: Turned written information into conversational podcast-style audio. Shut down May 2026 as larger platforms began offering similar experiences to large existing audiences.

fields.name: Yupp
fields.summary: Free playground comparing 800+ AI models side by side; never found PMF.
fields.narrative: Users could compare responses from hundreds of models (OpenAI, Google, Anthropic...), vote, and earn crypto. Founders said it never achieved strong enough product-market fit. Shut down March 2026.

fields.name: Figgs AI
fields.summary: Customizable AI characters for role-play; 1M+ users, too expensive to keep free.
fields.narrative: Ran 2023–2024, drew more than 1 million users, but developers said keeping the service free became too expensive to sustain.
